title: Make the Enemy Difficulty Curve readable without a mouse
body:
## Summary
DifficultyChart exposes its per-level values only through mouse-hover rects; keyboard and screen-reader users get no values and no zone verdicts.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:91-101 renders 50 transparent <rect onMouseEnter> targets; the tooltip (lines 57-89) is the only place the numeric value and zone (DANGER/SWEET SPOT/TRIVIAL) appear. The <svg> (line 33) has no role, aria-label or <title>, no element is focusable, and the three series are distinguished by hue only (legend swatches lines 103-109). Fixed looks like: focusable chart (tabIndex=0) with ArrowLeft/Right moving hoverLevel, an aria-live summary of the current level, role="img" + aria-label naming the series, and a non-hue channel (dash pattern) per series.

## Flow
- Tab through the Encounters tab -> focus never lands on the chart
- screen reader reads the svg as an unlabelled graphic -> no values
- build: tabIndex + onKeyDown stepping hoverLevel, aria-live region, role/aria-label, strokeDasharray per series

## Expected impact
Keyboard/AT users can read the difficulty values; measured by a render test. Risk: hover behaviour must stay identical for mouse users.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - difficulty values reachable by keyboard and AT
Before: 0 of 50 levels reachable by keyboard; 0 accessible names on the svg; 3 series distinguished by hue only
After: predicted 50 of 50 levels via ArrowLeft/Right, 1 accessible name, 3 distinct dash patterns
Method: simulation - counted from source; the after figure needs the change built and a render test, larger than this round's S budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:33 <svg width={CHART_W} height={200} ...> (no role/aria)
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:91-101 rect ... onMouseEnter={() => setHoverLevel(level)} (only interaction)
instrument: vitest render test: focus chart, fireEvent.keyDown ArrowRight x49, assert aria-live text names Lv50 and each series value; assert svg has role=img + aria-label

title: DifficultyChart letterboxes 40% of its height as blank space
body:
## Summary
The difficulty chart svg is 280x200 CSS px over a 280x120 viewBox, so the plot is drawn at scale 1 with 80px of empty band around it.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:33 sets width={CHART_W} (280) height={200} with viewBox 0 0 280 120 and class max-w-[280px]. Default preserveAspectRatio (xMidYMid meet) scales by min(280/280, 200/120) = 1, centring the 120-unit plot in 200px: 80px (40%) of the panel is blank. The wrapper also carries min-h-[200px] (line 32). Fix: height={CHART_H} (or scale the viewBox to the box) so the plot fills its panel, and align the wrapper min-height.

## Flow
- open Bestiary > Encounters
- Enemy Difficulty Curve panel shows the plot floating in a tall empty box
- fix: svg height = viewBox height (or widen viewBox), align wrapper min-h

## Expected impact
Designers see a tighter chart; measured by svg aspect vs viewBox aspect. Risk: the panel shrinks by 80px, shifting the layout below it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - chart fills its panel
Before: svg aspect 280:200 vs viewBox 280:120 -> 80 of 200 px blank (40%)
After: predicted 0 px blank (aspects equal)
Method: simulation - geometry computed from the attributes; no browser render in this round (no dev server allowed)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:20 const CHART_W = 280, CHART_H = 120
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:33 <svg width={CHART_W} height={200} viewBox={`0 0 ${CHART_W} ${CHART_H}`} className="w-full max-w-[280px]"
instrument: render test asserting svg width/height ratio equals viewBox ratio, plus a screenshot of the panel before/after

title: Derive encounter series labels and colours from ARCHETYPES by id
body:
## Summary
The difficulty-curve series and KILL_DEATH_STATS re-type the label and colour of archetypes ARCHETYPES already defines; they agree today only by copy.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersTab.tsx:61-65 hand-writes { label: 'Grunt', color: ACCENT_RED } / 'Caster' ACCENT_PURPLE_BOLD / 'Brute' MODULE_COLORS.content, which duplicate UI_META colours for melee-grunt / ranged-caster / brute (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts UI_META). src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts KILL_DEATH_STATS repeats label+color for the same 4 ids (melee-grunt, ranged-caster, brute, elite-knight) that DERIVED_ARCHETYPES carries. 14 hand-copied identity fields (3 series labels + 3 series colours + 4 labels + 4 colours) must track the roster; the next recolour in UI_META silently forks the encounter charts (data-viz encoding-vocabulary: identity-survives-reuse). Fix: key DIFFICULTY_* and KILL_DEATH_STATS by archetype id and resolve label/colour from ARCHETYPES.

## Flow
- recolour brute in UI_META
- archetype cards change; difficulty curve and kill/death cards keep the old colour
- fix: series = [{ id: "melee-grunt", data }], resolve label/colour from ARCHETYPES; parity test

## Expected impact
One edit recolours/renames an archetype everywhere. Risk: KillDeathStats is rendered by ArchetypesTab (sibling context bestiary-archetypes-ai), so its output must stay identical today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one owner for archetype identity on encounter charts
Before: 14 hand-copied label/colour fields; 0 tests pin their agreement
After: predicted 0 copied fields; a parity test fails on any drift
Method: simulation - fields counted in source; the change spans data.ts + EncountersTab + KillDeathStats (consumed by a sibling context) so it needs its own gated run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersTab.tsx:61-65 { label: 'Grunt', data: DIFFICULTY_GRUNT, color: ACCENT_RED } ...
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts KILL_DEATH_STATS: { id: 'melee-grunt', label: 'Forest Grunt', color: ACCENT_RED, ... } x4
instrument: parity test: every encounter series / KILL_DEATH_STATS row has label and colour equal to the ARCHETYPES entry with the same id; seed a recolour to see it go red

title: Move encounter/metric micro-text from text-[10px] to the sanctioned meta token
body:
## Summary
12 sites in 10 files of this context use the arbitrary text-[10px] class, each tripping the legibility-floor lint warning, instead of the sanctioned 10px meta tier (TEXT_SCALE.meta / text-2xs) or MicroLabel.

## Description
src/lib/typography-scale.ts sanctions 10px only through TEXT_SCALE.meta (text-2xs); the eslint no-restricted-syntax rule warns on text-[10px] literals. All 9 metric chips (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/metrics/*.tsx) and EncountersTab (3 sites) use the literal. Fix per site: text-2xs for dense meta (metric chips) or text-xs where it is reading text (wave-row tier/area, spawn role legend).

## Flow
- npx eslint on metrics/*.tsx and encounters/EncountersTab.tsx -> 12 legibility warnings
- replace each literal with TEXT_SCALE.meta / text-xs per the classify-per-occurrence rule
- re-run eslint -> 0

## Expected impact
Lint warnings for this context drop to 0 and the feature-map chips use the token. Risk: chip widths grow where a site is promoted to 12px.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - micro-text through the type token
Before: 12 text-[10px] literals in 10 files; 12 eslint legibility warnings
After: predicted 0 literals, 0 warnings
Method: probe - counted by grep and eslint on the real files; a 10-file token migration is kept out of a single-round bulk edit by the incremental-migration rule
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn "text-\[10px\]" src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/{metrics,encounters} | wc -l -> 12 (10 files)
eslint: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/metrics/CardsMetric.tsx:46:22 warning Text below the 12px legibility floor
instrument: npx eslint <the 10 files> warning count before/after

title: Guard bestiary pie/donut and difficulty hover against degenerate inputs
body:
## Summary
DifficultyChart's hover throws on a series with no points, and the death-cause pie and role donut render nothing when one slice is 100%.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:59 nearest() calls pts.reduce(...) with no initial value - a series with data: [] throws TypeError on the first hover. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/KillDeathStats.tsx:91-107 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/metrics/CardsMetric.tsx draw each slice as an SVG arc from start to start+sweep; at sweep = 360 the endpoints coincide and the arc draws nothing, so a single-cause (or single-role) dataset paints an empty circle. Latent with today's static data, but these components take series/props and the catalog pipeline is moving bestiary views onto produced data.

## Flow
- render DifficultyChart with series [{ label, data: [], color }] and hover -> TypeError
- render the pie with one cause at 100% -> empty svg
- fix: skip empty series in nearest(); draw a full circle when sweep >= 359.99

## Expected impact
No crash or blank chart on edge-shaped data. Risk: none for current data.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - charts survive empty and single-slice data
Before: 2 of 2 degenerate inputs fail (1 throw, 1 blank)
After: predicted 0 of 2
Method: simulation - walked from source; DeathCausesPie is not exported, so the render probe needs a small prop seam first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/DifficultyChart.tsx:59 const nearest = (pts) => pts.reduce((a, b) => ...).value;
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/KillDeathStats.tsx:104 d={`M 32 32 L ${x1} ${y1} A 28 28 0 ${largeArc} 1 ${x2} ${y2} Z`}
instrument: render tests: DifficultyChart with an empty series + mouseEnter; pie/donut with a single 100% slice asserting a visible circle/path

title: Derive the Tactics Config chips from the tactics data
body:
## Summary
TacticsLegend hardcodes MaxSimultaneous '2' and FlankingEnabled 'true' next to a map whose roles come from TACTICS_ENEMIES; the two agree only by coincidence.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersSubparts.tsx:17-20 hand-writes { MaxSimultaneous: '2', FlankingEnabled: 'true' }; the map (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/TacticsMap.tsx) draws TACTICS_ENEMIES with 2 'attacking' and 1 'flanking'. Adding a third attacker leaves the config claiming 2. Fix: export TACTICS_CONFIG from data.ts and assert attacking count <= MaxSimultaneous, flanking present iff FlankingEnabled.

## Flow
- add an attacking enemy to TACTICS_ENEMIES
- map shows 3 attackers, config still says MaxSimultaneous 2
- fix: one TACTICS_CONFIG + invariant test

## Expected impact
The planner cannot contradict itself. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - config chip and map agree
Before: 2 hand-kept config values, 0 tests; agree today (2 attackers, 1 flanker)
After: predicted 0 hand-kept values, 1 invariant test
Method: simulation - today's values agree, so no red-before is reachable without seeding; the worker seeds a 3rd attacker
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: invariant test over TACTICS_CONFIG and TACTICS_ENEMIES, seeded red with a 3rd attacker

title: Label the bestiary encounter stats as sample data or wire a real source
body:
## Summary
Kill/Death Statistics, Death Causes and the Enemy Difficulty Curve show fixed literals (e.g. 1,247 spawns, 23 player kills) with no marker that they are illustrative, so a designer reads them as telemetry.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts KILL_DEATH_STATS (timesSpawned 1247, killsOnPlayer 23, avgLifespan '18.3s'), DEATH_CAUSES (45/30/15/10%) and DIFFICULTY_GRUNT/CASTER/BRUTE are static constants; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/KillDeathStats.tsx and DifficultyChart render them under 'Statistics' headings with no provenance line. The context says these views are 'used to validate encounter balance ... before committing to the catalog', so presenting invented figures as measured is a claim-provenance gap (separate from the recorded difficulty-band deviations, which concern thresholds). Options: (a) a visible 'Sample data' provenance strip now, (b) feed them from the combat simulator / pipeline_artifacts. Choosing between them is a product direction.

## Flow
- designer opens Archetypes > Kill/Death Statistics
- reads Stone Brute as danger #1 with 67 player kills
- no data source exists behind the number

## Expected impact
Balance decisions stop being made on invented numbers. Risk: (b) couples this UI to simulator output shape.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every shown statistic names its source
Before: 4 stat panels, 0 provenance markers, 0 live sources
After: unmeasurable until the direction (label vs wire) is chosen
Method: simulation - which source is authoritative is a product decision, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts KILL_DEATH_STATS / DEATH_CAUSES / DIFFICULTY_* literals
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/KillDeathStats.tsx:18 SectionHeader label="Kill/Death Statistics" (no source line)
